title: Scale Drawings & Similar Figures
description: Learn Scale Drawings and Similar Figures for Grade 7: identifying similar polygons, scale factors, area ratios and real-life applications.

topics.title: Identifying Similar Polygons
topics.concept:
Similar figures have the same shape but may differ in size.

Two conditions for similarity:

  1. All corresponding angles must be EQUAL
  2. All corresponding sides must be PROPORTIONAL (same scale factor k)

For triangles, if two angles match (AA rule), the triangles are automatically similar.

CheckSimilar?
Rectangles 4x6 and 8x12Yes: ratios 8/4=2 and 12/6=2 are equal
Triangles 30-60-90 and 30-70-80No: second angles differ (60 vs 70)
Any two squaresYes: all angles 90deg, sides always proportional
topics.visual:
SIMILAR TRIANGLES:

Triangle A (small)     Triangle B (large)
      C (50 deg)               C' (50 deg)
      /\                          /\
     /  \                        /  \
    / 60  \ 70               / 60  \ 70
   /________\               /________\
  A   8cm   B             A'   16cm   B'

Scale factor = 16/8 = 2
All corresponding angles equal: A=A', B=B', C=C'

examples.problem: Are rectangles with sides 4cm x 6cm and 8cm x 12cm similar?
examples.solution: Ratio of widths: 8/4=2. Ratio of lengths: 12/6=2. Both ratios are equal, so YES they are similar with scale factor 2.

examples.problem: A triangle has angles 30, 60, 90. Another has angles 30, 70, 80. Are they similar?
examples.solution: NO — corresponding angles do not all match (60 != 70 and 90 != 80).

recap: All corresponding angles must be equal
All side length ratios must equal the same scale factor k
For triangles: if 2 angles match (AA), automatically similar

topics.title: Area Ratio vs Side Length Ratio
topics.concept:
When two figures are similar with side length ratio = k, their areas have a squared relationship:

Area Ratio = k^2

Similarly, if you know the area ratio, the side length ratio = square root of the area ratio.

Side Ratio (k)Area Ratio (k^2)
1:21:4
1:31:9
2:54:25
topics.visual:
SCALE FACTOR EFFECT ON AREA:

Square 1 (k=1)    Square 2 (k=2)    Square 3 (k=3)
  1cm x 1cm        2cm x 2cm         3cm x 3cm
  Area = 1cm^2     Area = 4cm^2      Area = 9cm^2

  k=2 -> Area ratio = 4 = 2^2
  k=3 -> Area ratio = 9 = 3^2

examples.problem: Triangle A has side 4cm, similar triangle B has side 12cm. Area of A = 8cm^2. Find area of B.
examples.solution: k = 12/4 = 3. Area ratio = 3^2 = 9. Area of B = 8 x 9 = 72cm^2.

examples.problem: Two similar hexagons have areas 25cm^2 and 100cm^2. Find the side length ratio.
examples.solution: Area ratio = 100/25 = 4. k^2 = 4, so k = 2. Side ratio = 1:2.

recap: Side ratio k -> Area ratio k^2
Area ratio -> Side ratio = square root of area ratio
Scale factor applies to all linear measurements (sides, perimeter, height)
Area scales with the square of the scale factor

online.title: Online Test — Chapter 7: Scale Drawings & Similar Figures

questions.q: Two triangles have angles 45, 65, 70 and 45, 65, 70. Are they similar?
questions.explanation: All corresponding angles are equal, so the triangles are similar by AA.

questions.q: Rectangle A: 5cm x 8cm. Rectangle B: 15cm x 24cm. What is the scale factor from A to B?
Two similar triangles have side ratio 2:5. What is their area ratio?
Triangle P ~ Triangle Q. PQ=6cm, AB=18cm. Area of P = 12cm^2. Find area of Q.
questions.explanation: k = 18/6 = 3. Area ratio = k^2 = 9. Area Q = 12 x 9 = 108 cm^2.

questions.q: A map scale is 1:100,000. Two cities are 5 cm apart on the map. What is the actual distance?
Two similar pentagons have areas 36cm^2 and 81cm^2. What is the side length ratio?
questions.explanation: Area ratio = 81/36 = 9/4. So k^2=9/4, k=3/2. Side ratio = 2:3.

questions.q: A model airplane is 1:72 scale. The real wingspan is 18m. What is the model's wingspan?
Triangle sides: 3cm, 4cm, 5cm. A similar triangle has smallest side = 9cm. Find perimeter of the larger triangle.
questions.explanation: k = 9/3 = 3. Original perimeter = 12 cm. Larger perimeter = 12 x 3 = 36 cm.

questions.q: A photo 4 x 6 inches is enlarged to 8 x 12 inches. By what factor does the area increase?
questions.explanation: k=2 (linear scale). Area increases by k^2=4. Or: old area=24, new area=96, ratio=4.

questions.q: Two circles are similar. Small radius=2cm, large radius=6cm. Area of small = 12.56cm^2. Find area of large circle.
questions.explanation: k=3, area ratio=9. Area large = 12.56 x 9 = 113.04 cm^2.

questions.q: Two similar triangles have areas 50cm^2 and 98cm^2. Find the ratio of their perimeters.
questions.explanation: Area ratio=98/50=49/25. Scale factor k=7/5. Perimeter ratio equals scale factor = 5:7 (smaller:larger).

questions.q: Triangle ABC ~ Triangle DEF. AB=8cm, BC=10cm, AC=12cm, DE=12cm. Find EF.
questions.explanation: Scale factor k = DE/AB = 12/8 = 1.5. EF corresponds to BC, so EF = 10 x 1.5 = 15 cm.

questions.q: A rectangular garden 20m x 15m is drawn on a plan with scale 1:200. Find the area on the plan in cm^2.
Two similar parallelograms have side ratio 3:4. The smaller has area 54cm^2. Find the larger area.
questions.explanation: Area ratio = 9:16. Larger area = 54 x (16/9) = 96 cm^2.

questions.q: A flagpole casts a 6m shadow. At the same time, a 1.5m stick casts a 2m shadow. Find the flagpole height.
questions.explanation: Similar triangles: h/1.5 = 6/2 => h/1.5 = 3 => h = 4.5 m

questions.q: A square of side 6cm is enlarged by scale factor 2.5. How many complete small squares (6cm x 6cm) fit in the large square?
questions.explanation: Area small=36cm^2. Large side=6x2.5=15cm, area=225cm^2. Area ratio=225/36=6.25. So 6 complete small squares fit.
